title: Two Sum Indices
problem_statement: Given n integers and a target, find two different positions i < j whose values add up to the target. Print i and j (0-based) separated by a space. If several pairs exist print the one with the smallest j, then the smallest i. A pair is guaranteed to exist.
input_format: Line 1: n. Line 2: n integers. Line 3: target.

title: Contains Duplicate
problem_statement: Print YES if any value occurs at least twice in the array, otherwise NO.

title: Valid Anagram
problem_statement: Two lowercase words are anagrams if one can be rearranged into the other. Print YES or NO.

title: Best Time to Trade
problem_statement: Given the price of a stock on each day, you may buy on one day and sell on a later day. Print the maximum profit, or 0 if no profit is possible.

title: Missing Number
problem_statement: An array holds n distinct numbers taken from 0..n. Exactly one number of that range is missing. Print it.

title: Single Number
problem_statement: Every value appears exactly twice except one that appears once. Print that value.

title: Move Zeroes
problem_statement: Move all zeroes to the end of the array while keeping the order of the other values. Print the resulting array.

title: Merge Two Sorted Arrays
problem_statement: Merge two sorted (ascending) arrays into one sorted array and print it.
input_format: Line 1: n, line 2: n integers. Line 3: m, line 4: m integers (an empty array is an empty line).

title: Majority Element
problem_statement: One value appears more than n/2 times. Print it.

title: Rotate Array
problem_statement: Rotate the array to the right by k positions and print the result.
input_format: Line 1: n. Line 2: n integers. Line 3: k.

title: Product of Array Except Self
problem_statement: For each position print the product of all other values. Use the fact that the answer fits in 64 bits; do not use division.

title: Container With Most Water
problem_statement: Each number is the height of a vertical line at positions 0..n-1. Choose two lines; the water held is the smaller height times the distance between them. Print the maximum.

title: Three Sum Count
problem_statement: Count the distinct value triplets (a, b, c) taken from different positions with a + b + c = 0. Triplets that use the same values in a different order count once.

title: Maximum Product Subarray
problem_statement: Find the largest product of any contiguous, non-empty subarray.

title: Trapping Rain Water
problem_statement: Each number is the height of a bar of width 1. After rain, water collects between the bars. Print how many units of water are trapped.

title: Sliding Window Maximum
problem_statement: Slide a window of size k from left to right over the array. Print the maximum of each window position.
input_format: Line 1: n. Line 2: n integers. Line 3: k.

title: Jump Game
problem_statement: Each value is the maximum jump length from that position. Starting at index 0, print YES if you can reach the last index, otherwise NO.
input_format: Line 1: n. Line 2: n non-negative integers.

title: Merge Intervals
problem_statement: Merge all overlapping intervals (touching endpoints count as overlapping). Print the merged intervals sorted by start, one per line as 'start end'.
input_format: Line 1: n. Then n lines: start end.

title: Kth Largest Element
problem_statement: Print the k-th largest value (counting duplicates) of the array.
input_format: Line 1: n. Line 2: n integers. Line 3: k.

title: Daily Temperatures
problem_statement: For each day print how many days you must wait for a warmer temperature, or 0 if none will come.

title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
problem_statement: Bars of width 1 have the given heights. Print the area of the largest rectangle that fits inside the histogram.

title: Reverse Words
problem_statement: Reverse the order of the words in a line. Words are separated by one or more spaces; print them separated by a single space.

title: Longest Common Prefix
problem_statement: Print the longest common prefix of the given words, or the single word NONE if they share no prefix.
input_format: Line 1: n. Then n lines, one word each.

title: Roman to Integer
problem_statement: Convert a Roman numeral (I, V, X, L, C, D, M with the usual subtractive forms such as IV and IX) to an integer.

title: First Unique Character
problem_statement: Print the 0-based index of the first character that occurs exactly once in the word, or -1 if there is none.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeats
problem_statement: Print the length of the longest substring in which no character repeats.

title: Longest Palindromic Substring Length
problem_statement: Print the length of the longest substring that reads the same forwards and backwards.

title: Group Anagrams Count
problem_statement: Words are in the same group when they are anagrams of each other. Print the number of groups.
input_format: Line 1: n. Then n lines, one word each.

title: Generate Parentheses
problem_statement: Print every well-formed string made of n pairs of parentheses, in alphabetical order (where '(' sorts before ')'), one per line.

title: Decode Ways
problem_statement: A message of digits is decoded by mapping 1->A, 2->B, ..., 26->Z. Print the number of different ways to decode the digit string.

title: Word Break
problem_statement: Given a dictionary of words and a string, print YES if the string can be split into a sequence of dictionary words (words may be reused), otherwise NO.
input_format: Line 1: the string. Line 2: m. Then m lines: dictionary words.

title: Edit Distance
problem_statement: Print the minimum number of single-character insertions, deletions or replacements needed to turn the first word into the second.
input_format: Two lines: word1, word2 (either may be empty).

title: Power of Two
problem_statement: Print YES if the integer is a positive power of two (1, 2, 4, 8, ...), otherwise NO.

title: Count Primes
problem_statement: Print how many prime numbers are strictly less than n.

title: GCD and LCM
problem_statement: Print the greatest common divisor and the least common multiple of two positive integers, separated by a space.
input_format: Two integers a b on one line.

title: Plus One
problem_statement: A non-negative integer is given as a list of its decimal digits, most significant first. Add one and print the digits separated by spaces.

title: Pascal Row
problem_statement: Print row r (0-based) of Pascal's triangle, values separated by spaces.

title: House Robber
problem_statement: Houses in a row hold the given amounts of money. You cannot rob two adjacent houses. Print the maximum you can take.

title: Coin Change Minimum
problem_statement: Given coin values (unlimited supply of each) and an amount, print the fewest coins that make exactly that amount, or -1 if impossible.
input_format: Line 1: n coins. Line 2: the n values. Line 3: amount.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
problem_statement: Print the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence (elements need not be adjacent).

title: Unique Paths
problem_statement: A robot starts at the top-left of an m x n grid and may only move right or down. Print the number of different paths to the bottom-right corner.

title: Climbing Stairs with Steps
problem_statement: You can climb 1 or 2 stairs at a time. Print the number of distinct ways to climb n stairs.

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
problem_statement: A sorted array of distinct integers was rotated at an unknown pivot. Print the index of the target, or -1 if absent. Aim for O(log n).
input_format: Line 1: n. Line 2: n integers. Line 3: target.

title: Number of Islands
problem_statement: A grid of 0s and 1s is given; 1 is land. Land cells connected horizontally or vertically form an island. Print the number of islands.
input_format: Line 1: rows cols. Then rows lines of cols characters (0 or 1).

title: Course Schedule
problem_statement: There are n courses (0..n-1) and p prerequisite pairs 'a b' meaning b must be taken before a. Print YES if all courses can be finished (no cycle), otherwise NO.
input_format: Line 1: n p. Then p lines: a b.

title: Shortest Path in a Maze
problem_statement: A maze grid has '.' open cells and '#' walls. Moving up, down, left or right, print the fewest steps from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell, or -1 if unreachable. Both corners are open.
input_format: Line 1: rows cols. Then rows lines of the grid.

title: N-Queens Count
problem_statement: Print the number of ways to place n queens on an n x n board so that no two attack each other.

title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
problem_statement: Two sorted arrays are given. Print the median of all their elements combined, with exactly one digit after the decimal point.
input_format: Line 1: n, line 2: n integers. Line 3: m, line 4: m integers. n+m >= 1 (an empty array has an empty line).
